hints.title: Continuous Range Coalescing
hints.text: Adding incoming numbers into an ordered collection of non-overlapping spans requires checking whether adjacent spans can be merged together.

hints.title: Ordered Interval Insertion Points
hints.text: Locate where the new value falls relative to existing disjoint intervals. Determine whether it extends the left neighbor, connects to the right neighbor, bridges both, or forms a new unit range.

hints.title: Four-Way Merge Blueprint
hints.text: Locate insertion index using bisect. If already covered by left interval, return early. Check left_merge (left.end + 1 == val) and right_merge (right.start - 1 == val). Merge both by expanding left and removing right, or extend either, or insert [val, val].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of active disjoint intervals
complexity.notes: Bisection lookup takes O(log N) while array shifting takes O(N) worst-case.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Rebuilding and sorting all discrete integers from scratch takes O(K log K) per query.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing only boundary pairs minimizes memory footprint while supporting fast consecutive coalescing.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Accurate boundary detection and bridging when a single point bridges two neighboring intervals.

solutions.approach: Binary Search Insertion with Four-Way Interval Coalescing
